source.title: Registering for a Class at the Riverside Centre
source.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
source.article: The Riverside Centre opens registration for its spring pottery classes on Monday. Each class meets once a week for six weeks, and the fee includes clay and access to shared tools. New participants should fill in the online form and choose a preferred class time. A confirmation email will arrive within two working days if a place is available. When a class is full, the centre puts applicants on a waiting list in the order their forms were received. Staff contact people on that list if a place opens before the first session. Participants who need step-free access can contact the front desk before registering so staff can confirm which room is suitable.

exercises.prompt: In the sentence 'New participants should fill in the online form and choose a preferred class time,' what does 'fill in the online form' mean?

options.text: It means to complete the online form by writing the required information.
options.explanation: Correct because the context requires participants to provide their details.

options.text: It means to delete the online form from the website.
options.explanation: Wrong because deleting the form would prevent registration instead of completing it.

options.text: It means to forward the online form to someone else without completing it.
options.explanation: Wrong because forwarding without completing leaves the required information missing.

exercises.explanation: The phrase describes completing the form with the required details.

exercises.prompt: Choose the natural and grammatically correct sentence using 'fill in the online form'.

options.text: Please fill in the online form before Friday to reserve your place.
options.explanation: Correct because the verb forms and infinitive 'to reserve' are natural and accurate.

options.text: Please fill in the online form before Friday to reserving your place.
options.explanation: Wrong because 'to reserving' should be 'to reserve'.

options.text: She has fill in the online form already.
options.explanation: Wrong because 'has fill' should be 'has filled'.

exercises.explanation: Only one sentence uses the phrase with correct grammar.

exercises.prompt: In the sentence 'When a class is full, the centre puts applicants on a waiting list in the order their forms were received,' what does 'waiting list' mean?

options.text: It means a list of people who have already finished the course.
options.explanation: Wrong because people on the list have not started and are still waiting for a place.

options.text: It means a list of people waiting to be offered a place if one becomes available.
options.explanation: Correct because the list holds applicants in order until a place opens.

options.text: It means a list of tools that participants can share during class.
options.explanation: Wrong because the sentence is about applicants waiting for a place, not about tools.

exercises.explanation: The phrase describes ordered applicants waiting for an open place.

exercises.prompt: Choose the natural and grammatically correct sentence using 'waiting list'.

options.text: They put us on the waiting list until a place becomes available.
options.explanation: Correct because pronoun case and article use are natural and accurate.

options.text: They put we on the waiting list until a place becomes available.
options.explanation: Wrong because 'we' should be 'us' after the verb 'put'.

options.text: They put us on waiting list until a place becomes available.
options.explanation: Wrong because 'on waiting list' should be 'on the waiting list'.

exercises.explanation: Only one sentence uses the phrase with correct grammar.

exercises.prompt: You are helping a new colleague get a staff lunch card. Write a short message to the colleague (2-3 sentences) explaining what to do. Use the phrase 'fill in the online form'.
